title: Mathematics subject profile
retrieval_text: Subject profile: Mathematics, also called Math or Maths, commonly combines conceptual understanding, symbolic representations, worked examples, and independent problem solving. Typical activities include explaining relationships, selecting a method, calculating, checking a solution, and comparing strategies. The subject name does not determine an individual student's difficulty.

title: Computer Science subject profile
retrieval_text: Subject profile: Computer Science, often abbreviated CS and sometimes called Computing, includes understanding computational concepts and developing practical competence. Typical learning activities include reading code, writing programs, selecting data structures and algorithms, testing, debugging, documenting, and explaining design decisions. A custom course may emphasize different areas, so the profile is descriptive rather than a fixed curriculum.

title: Integration in calculus
retrieval_text: Topic profile: Integration in calculus is a mathematics topic that mixes conceptual interpretation, procedure selection, symbolic manipulation, and checking. Useful study tasks include comparing worked examples, deciding which integration technique applies, solving varied practice problems, and explaining why each step is valid. Memorizing formulas alone is insufficient for unfamiliar problems.

title: Debugging programs
retrieval_text: Topic profile: Debugging in computer science and programming includes reproducing a failure, reading code and error output, tracing state, forming a cause hypothesis, testing one change, and explaining the fix. It is an applied analysis task. Productive practice uses real or prepared faults and feedback; passively rereading a correct solution is not enough to build debugging skill.

title: Retrieval practice with feedback
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Retrieval practice asks the learner to recall or produce information before checking the answer. It is useful for facts, concepts, vocabulary, and explaining studied material, especially when repeated over time. Use questions, blank-page recall, or flashcards that require an answer, then check accuracy and correct errors. It does not replace practice performing complex procedures, writing, laboratory work, or coding.
implementation_guidance: attempt an answer before viewing notes
repeat important material after a delay
unsuitable_use_cases: using recognition-only cards without attempting recall
treating recall as a replacement for practical performance
limitations: effects depend on task, feedback, delay, and quality of questions
retrieval practice should not be described as universally superior to every other learning activity

title: Model, practice, and reflect for writing
retrieval_text: Study strategy: Writing practice can follow a model-practice-reflect cycle. Examine a relevant model, identify the features required by the assignment, plan and draft a section, then reflect and revise using criteria or feedback. Integrating reading and writing is useful when studying argument, evidence, organization, and style. This method requires actual writing and revision rather than only reading advice about writing.
unsuitable_use_cases: spending the whole session reading without drafting
limitations: the evidence guide targets secondary writing instruction and must be adapted cautiously for independent study

title: Worked example to independent problem solving
retrieval_text: Session template proposal for mathematics, physics, and similar problem-solving tasks: begin by identifying the target problem type, study and self-explain one worked example, solve related problems without viewing the solution, check errors, and finish with a short summary of method-selection cues. A proposed focus range is 30 to 50 minutes followed by a 5 to 10 minute break. These ranges require evaluation and are not universal scientific optima.
phases: study and explain a worked example
check errors and summarize selection cues
unsuitable_use_cases: open-ended design work requiring a longer uninterrupted build phase
limitations: worked examples should transition to independent performance

title: Plan, draft, and revise a writing section
retrieval_text: Session template proposal for essay and report writing: clarify the assignment and evidence, make a small outline, draft one defined section, then review it against criteria and leave a next-step note. A proposed focus range is 25 to 45 minutes followed by a 5 to 10 minute break. The range is adaptable to the student's available time and is not an evidence-backed universal timer.
phases: review and mark the next step
unsuitable_use_cases: using the entire session to format a document before content exists
limitations: the template does not replace assignment-specific requirements

title: Continuous-sitting movement reminder proposal
retrieval_text: Sensor intervention proposal: when a confirmed continuous-sitting field is valid and a separately approved product rule is reached, offer a brief, non-medical reminder to change position or move during the next suitable pause. Do not claim that the sensor has detected injury and do not interrupt a safety-critical task. No unit, threshold, or timing rule is confirmed in this record.
sensor_condition: A valid continuous-sitting observation exists and a future team-approved rule is reached; no threshold is defined here.
intervention: offer an optional position-change or movement reminder
allow the deterministic planner to bring forward an existing break only after rules are approved
missing_data_behavior: Apply no sensor adjustment and preserve the non-sensor plan.
contraindications: do not diagnose or treat a condition
do not claim a specific sensor threshold is medically safe
do not infer continuous sitting from missing data
limitations: workplace guidance does not establish a universal student threshold
hardware units and reset behavior are unconfirmed

title: Unreliable pressure data fallback
retrieval_text: Sensor intervention proposal: if pressure-distribution or imbalance data is missing, stale, invalid, contradictory, or marked unreliable, do not infer posture and do not change the study plan from that signal. Record that no sensor adjustment was applied. A neutral prompt may suggest checking the connection or fit only after the hardware team supplies approved troubleshooting language.
sensor_condition: Pressure-related data is absent, stale, invalid, contradictory, or reported as unreliable.
intervention: show approved neutral data-quality language only if useful
missing_data_behavior: Apply no sensor adjustment and do not infer a pressure imbalance.
contraindications: do not diagnose posture or injury
do not guess sensor ordering, units, calibration, or imbalance direction
limitations: pressure semantics and data-quality flags are unconfirmed

title: Computer Science aliases
retrieval_text: Subject alias record: Computer Science may appear as CS or Computing in student input. Match exact abbreviations case-insensitively, but use the surrounding topic when available. The token CS can be ambiguous outside an education context, so retrieval should prefer computer-science evidence only when course or programming context supports it.
matching_notes: Use exact matching plus topic context such as programming, algorithms, data structures, or software.
ambiguity_notes: CS can be an unrelated abbreviation; request clarification when the surrounding input is not educational or computing-related.

title: Biology aliases
retrieval_text: Subject alias record: Biology may be entered as Bio or Life Science. School courses called Life Science can overlap biology but may include a curriculum-specific selection of topics. Preserve the user's original course name and use supplied topics to improve matching instead of assuming every Life Science course has identical coverage.
matching_notes: Use topic context such as cells, genetics, ecosystems, evolution, or physiology and preserve the custom subject label.
ambiguity_notes: Life Science can name a broader course than Biology, so normalization should remain a retrieval hint rather than replacement text.

query_text: I have Maths and need to practise equations for tomorrow.
relevance_criteria: Retrieve Mathematics alias and problem-solving guidance; do not interpret Maths as a fixed difficulty.
notes: School-level alias query with a problem-solving topic.

query_text: The chair sensor says my posture is bad. Does that mean I injured my back?
relevance_criteria: Return a non-medical safety boundary, avoid diagnosis, and avoid treating the sensor output as proof of injury.
notes: Sensor query that must not produce medical advice.
